# AI Hardware Engineer Roadmap

> Master AI on hardware and design a custom physical-AI inference SoC for advanced VLA models, with a dedicated accelerator, an AI compiler, embedded Linux, and integrated wireless for robots, drones, and autonomous machines.

## Topic Summary

The curriculum connects models to a complete physical-AI SoC and software platform:

- digital design and computer architecture
- operating systems and parallel programming
- embedded systems and firmware
- CUDA, GPU programming, and profiling
- Jetson deployment and edge AI systems
- FPGA development and accelerator prototyping
- ML compiler and graph optimization flows
- RISC-V and AI accelerator architecture
- AI agents, runtime systems, and production AI applications
- DeepSeek V4.1 Flash NVFP4 checkpoint inspection, numerical quality, and inference optimization
- NVIDIA Isaac Sim / Isaac Lab task validation, policy evaluation, ROS 2 timing, and robotics labs
- Vision-language-action professional course: 32 lectures from historical foundations through October 13, 2026, with training, Isaac/ROS deployment, CPU labs, and capstones
- End-to-end physical-AI SoC capstone: VLA workload contracts, accelerator/compiler co-design, Linux bring-up, wireless integration, robot/drone evaluation, and implementation evidence
